hypotheses.claim: The current recurrence-decision slice can be represented by ordinary typed control/data IR without a FRANK-specific ClayCode primitive.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production parser/canonical IR/type/effect/evaluator integration requires an opaque host semantic escape or cannot represent a required frozen field/control distinction.

hypotheses.claim: Program semantic identity should include recurrence decision/control meaning while semantic-state, state-version and trace-root witnesses remain runtime input/receipt identities rather than one program hash.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production replay/compiler counterexample requires runtime witness identity to change program meaning or shows separation breaks deterministic replay.

hypotheses.claim: Mixed semantic epochs must fail/route closed before recurrence continuation.
support: mutation discriminator detected loss of epoch guard
hypotheses.falsifier: A verified production design safely composes mixed epochs with an explicit typed reconciliation semantics and no stale-state hazard.

hypotheses.claim: A backend-neutral recurrence decision IR can preserve decision semantics across interpreter and native lowerings.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production backend differential tests produce architecture-relevant mismatches under the same canonical IR and inputs.

counterhypotheses.claim: Current frontend/parser debt prevents the semantic slice from being expressible end-to-end despite proxy IR closure.
R8 trajectory/capacity fields expose missing numeric/record/type semantics when integrated with production ClayCode.
The recurrence policy itself is scientifically wrong even if ClayCode compiles it perfectly.
